subject: Hosted API: Data handling, retention and deletion details
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-systems.com>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: acme-security@acme-systems.com
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API: Data handling & deletion questions

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this. A few quick questions from our security team as part of a standard vendor review for our hosted API usage: 

- What is the default retention period for request/response payloads (including prompt + model output) in the hosted API?
- Are customer requests stored in backups or snapshots, and if so what is the retention window on backups?
- Can Redwood confirm whether hosted API customer data is ever used to improve models or training data?
- If a user requests deletion, what is the timeline and scope (primary store + backups)? Any exceptions for legal hold?
- Where is data physically stored for hosted customers (can you confirm US-only vs EU-only options)?
- Who has access to raw request content for debugging (SRE, support) and are there RBAC/audit logs for those accesses?

We'd appreciate a brief written response that we can attach to our security questionnaire. If you have a short one-page summary or diagram that outlines the flow + retention windows, that would be great.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Security Engineer
Acme Systems

From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-systems.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, acme-security@acme-systems.com
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API: Data handling & deletion questions

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; looping in Dev (cc) for the backup/deletion mechanics and the data-flow diagram. I've attached a short summary PDF as well.

- Default request/response retention: 30 days for hosted API logs (prompts + outputs) unless otherwise contracted.
- Backups/snapshots: backups are retained as described in the attached summary; primary retention is 30 days, backups may persist copies for durability — see Dev's note for timing.
- Model training: Redwood does not use hosted customer request data to train or improve models. Customer content is isolated and may be excluded from any telemetry used for product metrics.
- Deletion workflow: we accept deletion requests via support portal or an Admin API; primary stores are purged promptly (see Dev's SLA below). Backups follow a separate lifecycle. Legal holds or subpoena processes can delay deletion.
- Data residency: hosted customers can choose a processing region at account creation (US or EU). EU-only processing is available for customers who require it.
- Access controls: access to raw request content is strictly role-limited (SRE, Support when troubleshooting) and logged. We provide audit logs; RBAC via SSO + fine-grained IAM.

I'll let Dev add the technical specifics on RTO for deletion from backups, API endpoints, and which logs we retain longer for auditing. Attached: retention_policy_summary.pdf (one-page).

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Hi Liam — following up with the technical details you asked for. Quoting Hannah's summary above then expanding: 

> Default request/response retention: 30 days for hosted API logs (prompts + outputs) unless otherwise contracted.

Technical specifics: 
- Primary storage: 
  - Customer request payloads and transient inference artifacts are persisted in encrypted primary stores (at-rest AES-256) for 30 days by default to support debugging, billing, and ops.
  - Customers may request 0-days (no retention) or extended retention (90/365 days) under an enterprise addendum.
- Backups & snapshots: 
  - Backups are created for redundancy; automated snapshots are kept for incremental restore and disaster recovery. Standard backup retention window is 90 days. Backups are encrypted and geo-replicated per the region.
  - Deletion from backups: logical deletion marks are applied immediately; physical removal from backup media follows the backup retention policy and can take up to 90 days in standard hosted plans. For enterprise customers we offer accelerated backup purge (configurable down to 7 days) as part of a contractual SLA.
- Deletion process & timeline: 
  - Deletion request accepted via Admin API endpoint (/v1/admin/delete-requests) or support portal (support ticket link below). 
  - Primary stores: records are removed from active stores within 24 hours of a validated request.
  - Search indexes and caches: invalidated within 24 hours; ephemeral caches are cleared immediately.
  - Backups: subject to backup retention policy as above (standard: up to 90 days). Immediate purge of backups only available under enterprise plan or for customers with dedicated capacity/private deployments.
  - Legal hold / subpoenas: if a legal hold applies, deletion is deferred and we notify the customer with the legal basis.
- Training & model improvement: 
  - Hosted API customer content is not used to train Redwood models. We do collect aggregated telemetry for product performance; this telemetry excludes customer content or any PII.
- Data residency: 
  - Customers can elect US or EU processing regions at account setup. Data for an EU regional account is processed and stored in EU cloud regions only (no cross-border replication unless explicitly authorized).
- Access controls & auditability: 
  - Support and SRE access to raw request content is logged in our audit trail. Access is granted via RBAC tied to SSO groups and just-in-time approval for support sessions.
  - Audit logs are retained 365 days by default (searchable by admin roles).
- APIs & support: 
  - Admin delete API: POST /v1/admin/delete-requests (requires admin API key + signed request)
  - Support ticket: https://redwood.example.com/support/ticket/HD-78923 (use this to request expedited processing)

Attachments provided: data_flow_diagram.png (diagram showing primary store, snapshots, and purge flow).

If you need a statement with exact language for your vendor questionnaire, tell me which control IDs (e.g., "Retention of customer content") you need and I can produce a short formal response for each.

Thanks,

Thanks Hannah and Dev — this is helpful. A couple of follow ups: 

1) For our audit we need a signed attestation that Redwood does not use hosted customer content for model training. Can you provide a short signed statement (PDF) we can store?
2) We need confirmation in writing that for our EU-only tenant you can guarantee processing and storage entirely within EU cloud regions (no cross-border replication).
3) For backups: Acme's policy requires ability to guarantee deletion from backups within 90 days; you indicate standard is 90 days which is acceptable — can you confirm that you will notify us when the logical delete is applied and when physical purge is completed?

If you can send the attestation and a line-item answer we can attach to our vendor security questionnaire, we should be good to move forward. I'll open a DocuSign request for the attestation and route it to the security team.

Appreciate the quick response.
